title: Connect AI to Billions of Legal Documents — Simon Eskildsen, turbopuffer & Jacob Lauritzen, Legora
talk_summary: Legora describes migrating legal-document search from Elasticsearch/Postgres to turbopuffer, using namespace-per-project/tenant isolation and object-storage-native indexes. The transferable mechanisms are hot/cold memory tiering, minimizing retrieval round trips, and namespace-level separation for multi-tenancy/security.

takeaways.what_they_do: They put each project or jurisdiction in its own turbopuffer namespace so cold namespaces stay on object storage while hot ones are cached, avoiding mixed hot/cold partitions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the cold ones and the hot ones would land on the same ones and the partitions would get really really big
takeaways.numbers: P99 search/ingestion went from ~100ms to 20s before fix; 400M docs at migration; 70+ to 200 tenants

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep frequently used context near memory/SSD and rare cold documents on blob storage, accepting higher latency for cold deep-research queries.
takeaways.numbers: S3 P99 ~200ms per 1MB blob; SSD ~1ms; 10B vectors target

takeaways.what_they_do: They design retrieval to do as much work as possible in few round trips because object-storage reads have high P99 latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Everything in Turbopuffer is optimized around doing as much work in as few round trips as possible.
takeaways.numbers: S3 P99 ~200ms for 1MB blob; target ~3 round trips

takeaways.technique: Hybrid exact+semantic retrieval for review context
takeaways.what_they_do: They use real BM25 plus vector search; BM25 improved relevancy and latency over pgvector-only search.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we got BM25 real BM25 much better uh relevancy much better latencies
takeaways.numbers: Latency improved order of magnitude; P99 better than median

takeaways.what_they_do: Atomic separation at namespace/table level allows different encryption keys and buckets per tenant, including customer-managed keys and revocation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every single table could be encrypted with a different key. Every single namespace could be in a different bucket.

takeaways.technique: Single shared service with logical namespaces
takeaways.what_they_do: They replaced many Elasticsearch/Postgres clusters with one turbopuffer cluster using namespaces, reducing operational overhead.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we could just have a single turbo puffer cluster
